Beetroot Tempura flasher

Installs the firmware on an M-VAVE FM-1 over USB, using M-VAVE's own FM1 Open update code.

Version 1.1: stability fix

Version 1.0 could crackle and freeze when the CPU meter went red, and could fail to start on an FM-1 that reconnects to a phone over Bluetooth at power-on. 1.1 keeps the audio engine inside its time budget, leaves the FM-1's Bluetooth and USB memory untouched, and adds a limiter. Everyone on 1.0 should install 1.1.

An FM-1 won't start or keeps restarting
  1. Turn off Bluetooth on every phone, tablet or computer the FM-1 has been paired with, so nothing reconnects to it at power-on.
  2. Switch the FM-1 off, then on again while holding HOME. On 1.1 this opens a silent safe mode; on 1.0 it simply starts without the phone connection.
  3. Connect it by USB and install 1.1 below, or M-VAVE's own firmware from their workbench at open.m-vave.com.
  4. If the screen stays black and Connect finds nothing, tick "replace other firmware" in step 2 and try Connect again with the FM-1 plugged in. If it still isn't found, contact M-VAVE support: they have a recovery tool for the FM-1.

1 Choose the firmware

Select both files from your build folder build\dx7\: generated\FM1_OFFICIAL_OPEN.fwsc and build-identity.json.

2 Connect the FM-1

Plug the FM-1 into this computer with a USB data cable and switch it on. Close other MIDI apps and any other workbench tabs.

3 Before you flash

4 Flash

If anything goes wrong, leave the FM-1 connected and press Install again: the device stays in its update loader until a complete image is written. You can always return to FM1 Open or stock V15 from the M-VAVE workbench at open.m-vave.com.

5 Load sounds

Beetroot Tempura makes grains from the FM-1's eight sample slots, and the FM-1 holds about 19.5 seconds of sound across all eight. Pick a pack, or choose a sound for each track from the 28 in the library. Tap ▶ to hear one.

    Loading replaces the FM-1's whole sample bank. Back it up in the M-VAVE workbench first if it has sounds you want to keep. Your own WAVs can be loaded there too.
